The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 7m 44s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,194.52 USD {customer_loss}
- People who responded: 1 {responders}
- Their time, added together: 9 min {engineer_minutes}

What was done to end it:
- Some Person: resolved it from PagerDuty - "kept the flag off and paged the checkout team"
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - not judged by Argus (Some Person resolved it first), still in place

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 21:33 to 21:40:44 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 21:58:20 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 21:39:30 UTC
Ended by: Some Person from PagerDuty, Nov 12, 2026, 21:40:44 UTC - kept the flag off and paged the checkout team

Summary
The service broke at 21:33 UTC. Some Person reported the incident resolved at 21:40:44 UTC, 7 minutes 44 seconds later. 28.6% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.8% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,194.52 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - not judged, still in place. If anyone switches monthly-spend-feature back on before the spend-summary code is fixed, account pages could fail the same way again.

Impact
7m 44s - onset until reported resolved
40.5% - peak error rate
2,748 - requests failed
0.8% to 28.6% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,194.52 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The spend-summary code that monthly-spend-feature turns on raises a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 for some account page requests, and those requests fail with that error. The evidence does not show why the divisor is zero for those requests.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 36 minutes, 21:04–21:39; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 21:36
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 21:33–21:39
why 1 The requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, starting in the minute the incident began. Before that minute, the only account-page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 35 occurrences in 29 minutes, 21:04–21:32
why 2 That code ran because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at 21:33:31 UTC. The flag read off on every evaluation before that minute, was split between off and on during that minute, and read on for every evaluation after it.
  Evidence:
    P1 21:33:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 21:03–21:32
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 21:33
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 21:34–21:39
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or a revision change: no deploy came back from the window that was read, the flag change was the only production change read back, and account pages rendered normally with the running revision in place before the onset.
      T8 21:39:53 Investigator Agent: Read back 1 production change
      T9 21:39:53 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 27 minutes, 21:03–21:29
      G7e5d
    A different flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this one flag change by anyone other than Argus in the hour that was read.
      T14 21:39:56 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 21:39:56
    Shoppers closing their connections: these errors were logged while the service ran normally before the onset, and stopped being logged before it.
      G46bc
      Gad41
why 3 The code path behind the flag divides by a value that is zero for some account page requests, and those requests fail with the resulting error.
  Evidence:
    G5309
Contributing factors
- The flag was switched from off for all traffic to on for all traffic within a single minute. No staged rollout, and no automatic check of the error rate tied to the flag change, was seen. (AI-3)
- No test or pre-enablement check was seen that ran the spend-summary path with the flag on against account data that gives a zero divisor. (AI-4)
- No handling was seen that keeps an error in the spend-summary section from failing the whole account page. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 21:33:31 UTC. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% to 20-40%. | 0.93 | tried, not judged

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 21:33:31 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
Resolved by Some Person from PagerDuty, 21:40:44 UTC - kept the flag off and paged the checkout team
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 21:40:03 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | not judged, still in place

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 21:33 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 21:39:07 UTC, 6 minutes 7 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so that a zero divisor no longer raises an error. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-2 | Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is merged and deployed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Roll out feature flags in production to a small share of traffic first, and turn the flag off automatically if the error rate rises after the change. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Require that code behind a feature flag is tested with the flag on, including edge-case account data such as zero values, before the flag can be switched on in production. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Make the account page still render, without the spend summary, when the spend-summary section raises an error. | prevent | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 45 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 21:33.
- 49 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 56 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 1 minute 37 seconds after the alert was raised, Some Person moved the incident to RESOLVED from PagerDuty - kept the flag off and paged the checkout team.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

Response effort
9 min - engineer time, 1 responder
105,946 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/1f065115-c983-45d4-9e57-eaddef8bac1d
Changes to production read
P1 | 21:33:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 21:03–21:32
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 27 minutes, 21:03–21:29
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 35 occurrences in 29 minutes, 21:04–21:32
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 36 minutes, 21:04–21:39; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 21:36
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 21:33
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 21:33–21:39

Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12
- Shared page: the on-call incident this one was paged under was also about 2 other incidents, so the engineer minutes are its whole response rather than this incident's share

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  no candidate was confirmed
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages. Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates the incident cost the shop {customer_loss} in takings. The number of people who responded was {responders}, and their time added together came to {engineer_minutes}. Argus reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, and that change is still in place. Argus did not judge whether the revert worked, because Some Person resolved the incident first from PagerDuty, keeping the flag off and paging the checkout team.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
